content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Research group develops multivariate statistical process control and data-driven fault prognosis methods for condition monitoring of machinery using synchronized acquisition of multiple sensor modalities.","sources":[{"id":"R0822","field":"bio","quote":"multivariate statistical process control, and data-driven fault prognosis including remaining useful life estimation"}]},{"text":"Remaining useful life prediction using recurrent neural networks with long short-term memory achieves 14.3% mean absolute percentage error on bearing run-to-failure sequences and demonstrates practical guidance for cross-condition generalization with simple linear scaling.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-00593","field":"abstract","quote":"With 20 or more training sequences, mean absolute percentage error in RUL prediction stabilised near 14.3%"}]},{"text":"Particle filter frameworks for remaining useful life estimation construct state-space degradation models from experimental data and propagate measurement uncertainty through health indicators to produce confidence intervals rather than point estimates.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08928","field":"abstract","quote":"particle filter framework for estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of gearbox output-shaft bearings"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-08933","field":"abstract","quote":"propagating the uncertainty arising from sensor noise, mounting variability, and feature computation choices"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's group specializes in data-driven fault prognosis and remaining useful life estimation from multivariate sensor data [R0822], with published work on LSTM-based RUL prediction from time-series sequences [SYN-PUB-00593], particle filter degradation modeling [SYN-PUB-08928], and uncertainty quantification in prognostic estimates [SYN-PUB-08933]—all directly applicable to building a transformer failure scoring module from dissolved gas analysis and SCADA load data."}
